examples.request: Let users set a due date on tasks

steps.text:
- db/schema.sql: the tasks table has id, title, done, and created_at (TEXT). There is no due-date column.
- src/api/tasks.ts (POST /tasks): reads only title from the body and inserts done: 0 and created_at. A due date would be dropped here unless this handler is changed.
- src/api/tasks.ts (PATCH /tasks/:id): passes req.body straight to db.update, so a due-date field could be stored without validation. GET /tasks uses SELECT *, so a new column would be returned automatically.
- src/ui/TaskList.tsx: renders only a checkbox and the title for each li. It has no date display or date input.
- tests/e2e/README.md: no end-to-end tests exist. Unit tests cover only the db helpers, not the API or UI.

Gap: the Task type, the db helper code, any migration mechanism, and the date format or timezone convention are not in the provided text.

**User story**

As a task-list user, I want to set an optional due date on a task so that I can see when it needs to be done and plan my work around it.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Creating a task: POST /tasks accepts an optional due date alongside the title and stores it in a new nullable due-date column on the tasks table (added to db/schema.sql). Tasks created without a due date still work and store null.
2. Editing a task: PATCH /tasks/:id can set, change, or clear the due date. The handler rejects values that are not valid dates in the agreed format (it currently passes req.body straight to db.update with no validation), and the response returns an error the UI can show.
3. Reading tasks: GET /tasks returns the due date for each task (SELECT * already returns new columns), and existing tasks without a due date come back as null.
4. UI: In src/ui/TaskList.tsx, each task shows its due date next to the title when one is set, and the user can enter or change it with a date input. Tasks with no due date look as they do today.

**Open questions (not covered by the research)**
- Date format and timezone convention: date-only (YYYY-MM-DD) or full timestamp? created_at is TEXT, but its format is not in the provided text.
- Migration: no migration mechanism was found, so existing databases need a way to get the new column.
- The Task type and db helper code were not provided and will need to be updated to include the due date.
- Test coverage: no API or UI tests exist, so criteria 1 to 4 would need new tests.

**Data** - `db/schema.sql`: add `due_date TEXT NULL` to the `tasks` table (date-only `YYYY-MM-DD`; nullable so existing rows read back as null). - No migration mechanism exists: add `db/migrations/001_add_due_date.sql` with `ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN due_date TEXT;` and a small runner (or a one-time startup check in the db helper) that applies it to existing databases. - Update the `Task` type and db helper code (not in the research; locate alongside `src/api/tasks.ts`) to include `due_date: string | null`. **API** - `src/api/tasks.ts` POST `/tasks`: accept `{ title: string, due_date?: string | null }`, validate `due_date` against `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` plus a real-date check, insert it (null when absent) along with `done: 0` and `created_at`; respond `201 { id, title, done, due_date, created_at }`. - `src/api/tasks.ts` PATCH `/tasks/:id`: stop passing `req.body` straight to `db.update`; whitelist `{ title?, done?, due_date?: string | null }`, run the same date validation (null clears), and respond `400 { error: "due_date must be YYYY-MM-DD" }` on failure, otherwise `200` with the updated task. - GET `/tasks` is unchanged (`SELECT *` already returns `due_date`); add `tests/api/tasks.test.ts` covering create-with/without date, patch set/change/clear, invalid date rejection, and null on legacy rows. **UI** - `src/ui/TaskList.tsx`: extend the task shape with `due_date`, and in each `li` render `{task.due_date}` after the title only when set; tasks without a date render as today (checkbox + title). - Add `` per task that PATCHes `/tasks/:id` with `{ due_date }` (empty input sends `null` to clear); states: idle, saving (input disabled), error (show the API `error` text inline beside the input). - Add the same date input to the create form so POST `/tasks` sends `due_date`; add `tests/ui/TaskList.test.tsx` for display-when-set, no-display-when-null, and error state.

E2E: PASS

Flow 1: Create a task with a due date (UI form -> POST /tasks -> db -> GET /tasks -> list)
- User picks a date in the create form and submits. The UI POSTs { title, due_date: value || null }. PASS.
- The handler destructures due_date and validates it. "2026-03-15" passes the regex and the round-trip check. The row is inserted with due_date and returns 201 with the new field. PASS.
- The migration adds a nullable due_date column and schema.sql is updated. GET /tasks uses SELECT *, so the column comes back, and the list renders the date in a span next to the title. PASS.
- Create without a date: the UI sends null (or the field is omitted, so the default is null). validDate(null) is true, and null is stored. The `{t.due_date && ...}` check renders nothing, so the row looks as it does today. PASS.
- Invalid date such as "2026-02-30": the regex matches, but the round-trip check changes it to 03-02, so it is rejected with 400 and the error body. PASS.

Flow 2: Edit, change and clear a due date (DueInput -> PATCH /tasks/:id)
- User changes the date input. The UI PATCHes { due_date: "2026-04-01" }. The handler whitelists title, done and due_date, validates, and calls db.update. The response is 200 with the updated task. onSaved replaces the task in the list and the new date shows. PASS.
- User clears the input. The UI sends due_date: null. "due_date" in patch is true and validDate(null) is true, so the column is set to null. The span disappears. PASS.
- Server-side bad value (such as "abc" from a manual call): 400 with { error: "due_date must be YYYY-MM-DD" }. The UI reads body.error and shows it in role="alert". The input is re-enabled in finally. PASS.
- Network failure: the catch shows "Network error". PASS.
- A PATCH that does not touch due_date, such as toggling done, does not trigger date validation, so existing behaviour is preserved. PASS.

Flow 3: Existing data and empty state
- Legacy rows get NULL after the ALTER TABLE migration. GET /tasks returns null for them, and the UI shows no date and an empty date input (due_date ?? ""). PASS.
- An empty list renders "No tasks yet. Add one above." PASS.

Non-blocking notes (assumptions the author flagged, not broken flows):
- A missing id on PATCH may not return 404, because the author did not handle it and assumed the db.update signature. This is outside the acceptance criteria.
- The migration's run-once check at startup is described but not shown in code. It should be confirmed when integrating.
- The create-form code is described, not written out in full.
- The input is disabled while saving, but the controlled value only updates after the response. This is acceptable, because the value reverts to the stored date on error.

VERDICT: APPROVE

- All four criteria met: POST stores optional `due_date` (null default) in the new nullable column and schema.sql; PATCH whitelists `title`/`done`/`due_date`, validates the date (regex + round-trip, so "2026-02-30" is rejected) and returns a 400 with `{ error }` the UI shows in `role="alert"`; GET via `SELECT *` returns the column with null for legacy rows; the UI shows the date span only when set and offers a date input.
- Security: the key whitelist in PATCH fixes the previous "pass req.body straight to db.update" mass-assignment hole; date validation prevents junk strings in the column. `db.update(req.params.id, ...)` is assumed parameterized, as the existing helper already takes an id.
- Minor, non-blocking: PATCH with an unknown id is not 404-handled and `title`/`done` are still not type-checked (pre-existing behaviour, outside the story). Confirm the run-once migration guard (`PRAGMA table_info`) and the create-form date input when integrating, since both are described rather than fully written.

Add due dates to tasks

- **Data:** Add nullable `due_date TEXT` (YYYY-MM-DD) to `tasks` in `db/schema.sql`, with `db/migrations/001_add_due_date.sql` applied to existing databases by a startup check. `Task` type and db helper now carry `due_date: string | null`.
- **API:** POST `/tasks` accepts optional `due_date` and returns 201. PATCH `/tasks/:id` whitelists `title`, `done`, `due_date` (null clears) and returns 400 `{ error: "due_date must be YYYY-MM-DD" }` on bad input. Both validate format and real calendar date. GET unchanged.
- **UI:** `TaskList` shows the due date after the title only when set. Each task gets a `DueInput` (date input, disabled while saving, inline error) that PATCHes the task. Same input on the create form. Empty state kept.

examples.request: Add a priority label to each task

steps.text:
- `db/schema.sql`: the `tasks` table has `id`, `title`, `done` (INTEGER, default 0), and `created_at`. There is no priority column.
- `src/api/tasks.ts`: `GET /tasks` runs `SELECT * FROM tasks ORDER BY created_at DESC`. `POST /tasks` reads only `title` and inserts `done: 0` with a timestamp. `PATCH /tasks/:id` passes `req.body` straight to `db.update`, so a priority field would reach the DB without validation.
- `src/ui/TaskList.tsx`: `TaskList` renders each task as a checkbox plus its title inside an `<li>`. Nothing shows a priority, and the `Task` type it imports is not in the provided text.
- `tests/e2e/README.md`: there are no end-to-end tests. The README says unit tests cover only the db helpers, and those helpers are not in the provided text.
- `README.md`: a one-line description (Express API, SQLite, React UI). It does not document fields, allowed values, or a migration process.

Gaps: no migration mechanism or db helper code, no `Task` type definition, no allowed priority values or default, and no visible unit tests for the API or UI.

**User story**

As a user managing my to-do list, I want to assign a priority label to each task so that I can see at a glance which tasks matter most.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. The `tasks` table gets a `priority` column. Existing rows get a default value so current data stays valid. The allowed values and the default are not defined in the research and need to be decided (for example low, medium, high, default medium).
2. `POST /tasks` accepts an optional `priority` along with `title`. If it is missing, the default is stored. `PATCH /tasks/:id` rejects any priority outside the allowed values with a 400 error, since it currently passes `req.body` straight to `db.update` without validation.
3. `GET /tasks` returns `priority` for every task, and `TaskList` shows each task's priority label next to its title. The `Task` type, which is not in the provided text, is updated to include it.
4. Unit tests cover the validation and the default value. Because no end-to-end tests exist and the db helper code is not visible, the test scope for the db helpers and the UI needs to be confirmed.

**Open questions:** the migration approach (the research found no mechanism and no documented process), the allowed values and default, and whether the list should be sorted by priority. The current sort is by `created_at DESC`.

**Data**
`db/schema.sql`: add `priority TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium' CHECK (priority IN ('low','medium','high'))` to `tasks`. No migration mechanism exists, so ship a one-off `ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN priority TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium'` (run at startup if the column is missing; SQLite can't add a CHECK via ALTER, so enforce allowed values in the API). Existing rows get `'medium'`.

**API**
`src/api/tasks.ts`: add `PRIORITIES = ['low','medium','high'] as const` and an `isPriority()` guard. `POST /tasks` reads `{ title, priority? }` and inserts `priority ?? 'medium'`; `PATCH /tasks/:id` validates `req.body.priority` with the guard and returns `400 { error: 'invalid priority' }` before calling `db.update`. `GET /tasks` keeps `SELECT *` so `priority` comes through; sort stays `created_at DESC` until the open question is settled.

**UI**
Add `priority: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'` to the `Task` type (file not in the research; locate it where `src/ui/TaskList.tsx` imports it). In `TaskList.tsx`, render a `<span className="priority priority-{value}">` label after the title inside each `<li>`; states are the three values, no empty state needed since the default guarantees a value.

**Tests**
New `tests/api/tasks.test.ts`: `POST` without priority stores `'medium'`; `PATCH` with `'urgent'` returns 400; `PATCH` with `'high'` succeeds. DB-helper and UI test scope stays unconfirmed per the story.

E2E: PASS

Flow 1: Create a task with a priority and see it in the list. PASS
- POST /tasks with {title, priority:'high'}: isPriority accepts it, and db.insert stores priority 'high'.
- POST with no priority: the check is skipped, 'medium' is stored.
- GET /tasks runs SELECT * and returns the priority column, so the Task type matches the payload.
- TaskList reads t.priority, looks up LABELS, and renders "High" in span.priority-high next to the title.
- The loading, error and empty states render in the right order (error, then null, then empty, then list).

Flow 2: An existing database upgrades and old tasks still show a label. PASS
- On startup, PRAGMA table_info finds no priority column, so the ALTER ... DEFAULT 'medium' runs. This is idempotent: it is skipped once the column exists.
- Existing rows get 'medium' because the column is NOT NULL with a default.
- GET returns the old rows with 'medium', and the UI shows "Medium". The fallback also covers any stale response that lacks the field.
- Fresh installs use schema.sql with the CHECK constraint. Migrated databases have no CHECK, but API validation on POST and PATCH covers that gap.

Flow 3: Update a task's priority, including a bad value. PASS
- PATCH with priority 'urgent' (or null, or a number) fails the isPriority check and returns 400 {error:'invalid priority'}. The row is unchanged.
- PATCH with 'low' passes validation and goes to db.update. The next GET returns 'low', and the UI shows "Low".
- PATCH without priority skips the check, so existing title-only updates still work.

Non-blocking notes:
- The db.insert and db.update helpers, and the real path of the Task type, are not visible. The flows assume the helpers pass the fields through unchanged.
- PATCH still passes req.body straight to db.update, so any other fields are still writable. This was already the case before this story and is not part of it.

VERDICT: APPROVE

- AC1 met: `priority TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium'` with CHECK in schema.sql and an idempotent PRAGMA-guarded ALTER for existing DBs; values low/medium/high, default medium are decided and documented.
- AC2 met: POST stores `priority ?? 'medium'` and PATCH returns 400 via `isPriority` for any non-allowed value; POST validation closes the no-CHECK gap on migrated databases. No injection risk (parameterized helpers, no string-built SQL from input).
- AC3 met: `SELECT *` returns the new column, `Task` type includes `priority: Priority`, and `TaskList` renders `LABELS[p]` next to the title with a safe fallback; E2E flows 1-3 pass.
- AC4 partially unconfirmed as the story itself allows: no unit test code is shown for validation/default, and the `Task` type path is a guess. Not blocking, but add the two tests (400 on bad priority, 'medium' when omitted) and fix the import path on merge. PATCH still forwards whole `req.body` to `db.update` (pre-existing mass-assignment surface, out of scope).

**Add priority label (low/medium/high) to each task**

- **Data:** Add `priority` column to `tasks` (default `'medium'`, CHECK low/medium/high) with an idempotent startup `ALTER TABLE` guarded by `PRAGMA table_info`; existing rows become `'medium'`.
- **API:** `POST /tasks` accepts optional `priority` (defaults to `'medium'`); `PATCH /tasks/:id` validates via `isPriority()` and returns `400 { error: 'invalid priority' }` on bad values; `GET /tasks` unchanged.
- **UI:** `priority` added to the `Task` type; `TaskList.tsx` renders `<span className="priority priority-{value}">` after the title, with a fallback to `'medium'` and loading, error and empty states.

examples.request: Add a search box to filter tasks

steps.text:
- src/api/tasks.ts: GET /tasks runs SELECT * FROM tasks ORDER BY created_at DESC with no parameters and ignores req.query. Any title filter would have to go through this route or the SQL it runs.
- db/schema.sql: the tasks table has id, title (TEXT, NOT NULL), done (INTEGER, default 0), and created_at (TEXT). title is the only text column a search would match on.
- src/ui/TaskList.tsx: TaskList({ tasks }) renders each task as a checkbox and its title, with no input, state, or filtering. It receives an already-fetched tasks array.
- README.md: describes the project as an Express API, SQLite, and a React UI. It does not mention search or filtering.
- tests/e2e/README.md: there are no end-to-end tests. Unit tests cover only the db helpers, so nothing covers the tasks route or TaskList.
- Gaps: the parent component that fetches tasks and holds state, the db.all helper signature (including whether it accepts bound parameters), and any existing unit tests for the db helpers are not in the provided text.

As a person managing a long task list, I want a search box that filters my tasks by title so that I can find a specific task quickly without scrolling through the whole list.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A text search box appears above the task list in the React UI. As I type, only tasks whose title contains the typed text are shown. Matching is case-insensitive, and the checkbox and title display is unchanged.
2. Clearing the search box shows the full list again, still ordered by created_at descending.
3. When no task title matches, the list shows a "No tasks match" message instead of a blank area.
4. Filtering matches on the title column only. Filtering does not change or lose any task's done state.

Open items to settle before building (not in the research): where the filter runs, either in the UI over the already-fetched tasks array or server-side by having GET /tasks read a query parameter and bind it into the SQL (this depends on whether db.all accepts bound parameters); and which parent component holds the search state.

Data: No migration. `db/schema.sql` tasks table already has `title TEXT NOT NULL`, `done INTEGER DEFAULT 0`, `created_at TEXT`; filter reads existing `title` column only.

API: No new endpoint. `GET /tasks` in `src/api/tasks.ts` stays `SELECT * FROM tasks ORDER BY created_at DESC`, returning `{ id, title, done, created_at }[]`; filter runs in the UI over the fetched array, so the unknown `db.all` bound-parameter signature is not a dependency. Add server-side `?q=` later only if the list outgrows client filtering.

UI: Add `search: string` state (`useState("")`) in the parent that fetches tasks (name unknown; likely `src/ui/App.tsx`, confirm before building) and pass `tasks.filter(t => t.title.toLowerCase().includes(search.toLowerCase()))` to `TaskList`. New `src/ui/SearchBox.tsx`: controlled `<input type="text">` rendered above `TaskList`, with placeholder "Search tasks". `src/ui/TaskList.tsx`: when `tasks.length === 0` render "No tasks match"; checkbox and title rendering unchanged; done toggling unchanged because filtering only derives a view and never mutates the source array.

No migration is needed and no API route changes: filtering runs client-side in the UI, so `GET /tasks` stays as it is.

```sql
-- db/migrations: none. tasks(title TEXT NOT NULL, done INTEGER DEFAULT 0, created_at TEXT) already covers the filter.
```

```ts
// src/api/tasks.ts (unchanged)
router.get("/tasks", (req, res) =>
  res.json(db.all("SELECT * FROM tasks ORDER BY created_at DESC")));
// returns { id, title, done, created_at }[]
```

Notes: Add a server-side `?q=` later only if the list outgrows client filtering, and then confirm the `db.all` bound-parameter signature first.

E2E: PASS

Flow 1: Type in the search box and filter by title (AC1, AC4). The review is on the supplied code only.
- PASS: App fetches tasks through the unchanged `GET /tasks`, which returns `{id, title, done, created_at}[]` ordered by `created_at` DESC. When loading and error are both false, App renders `SearchBox` above `TaskList`.
- PASS: Typing "rep" calls `onChange`, which sets `search`. `q` is the trimmed, lowercased text, and `visible` keeps tasks whose lowercased title includes `q`. This is case-insensitive and matches on the title only. `TaskList` renders the existing checkbox and title for each visible task.
- PASS: `filter` keeps each task object as is, so `done` is untouched. Toggling a checkbox on a filtered row uses the existing handler, so done state is not lost when the search changes.

- PASS: With `search` set to "", `q` is "" and `includes("")` is true for every title. The full list returns, and `filter` keeps the fetched order, so it is still `created_at` descending.
- PASS: A whitespace-only query trims to "" and shows the full list, which is reasonable behavior.

Flow 3: A search that matches nothing (AC3).
- PASS: Typing "zzz" gives an empty `visible` and `isFiltered=true`, so `TaskList` returns "No tasks match" instead of a blank area.
- PASS: With no tasks and no search, the list shows "No tasks yet". This is a separate state and does not conflict with the acceptance criteria.

- Security/data safety: no new API surface, no SQL change, no user input reaches the server or DOM as raw HTML (React escapes), no persistence of search state. No real risk.

Add search box to filter tasks by title
